sources.title: Andrew Baker, Hopf algebras over fields: an introduction, SMSTC supplementary course notes 2026–7
sources.locator: Complete 55-page notes; read §§2.22–2.25 (printed pp.30–31), §3.2 (printed pp.38–39), §3.4 (printed p.40), and §3.12 (printed pp.47–48).

contents.name: §2.22 Hopf homomorphisms preserve antipodes; §2.23 Hopf ideal definition; §2.24 quotient Hopf algebra; §2.25 kernels of Hopf maps
contents.reason: These sections give the standard ideal/coideal/antipode-stability conditions and quotient and kernel conclusions; the carrier supplies full proofs for the quotient identities, universal property, and tensor-kernel branch.

contents.name: §3.2 Example 3.2: the divided-power Hopf algebra and the stated relationship with the finite dual of the polynomial Hopf algebra
contents.reason: This source claim is not used: its stated k[X]° ≅ Γ_k relationship appears to omit nonzero-point evaluation functionals permitted by the source's own cofinite-ideal definition. The assigned carrier proves its point-indexed formula directly by ideal factorization and CRT; owner reconciliation of the source convention is recorded in batch notes.

contents.name: §3.4 group algebras and dual group algebras, including formulas on the group and Dirac-function bases
contents.reason: The local example independently evaluates the transposed product, coproduct, counit, and antipode on the finite group and Dirac-function bases.

contents.name: §3.12 Taft algebras H_{n,ζ}: presentation, structure maps, and the g^i x^j basis
contents.reason: The section supplies a comparison for the Taft presentation and formulas; the local proof derives the PBW basis and verifies every Hopf relation, accounting for the inverse parameter convention.

contents.name: §3.12 specialization n=2, ζ=-1: four-dimensional noncommutative and noncocommutative example
contents.reason: The local specialization checks the characteristic hypothesis, the four basis elements, and both failures using the tensor-product basis.

sources.title: Kalle Kytölä, Introduction to Hopf algebras and representations, University of Helsinki lecture notes, Spring 2011
sources.locator: Complete 91-page notes; read all of §§3.8–3.9 (printed pp.47–52), including Theorems 3.45–3.46 and their preparations.

contents.name: §3.8 equation (3.8): representative forms of finite-dimensional algebra modules
contents.reason: The local coefficient proof constructs the quotient regular module and proves both directions of the finite-dimensional matrix-coefficient characterization.

contents.name: §3.9 Definition 3.43 and Example 3.44: restricted dual and representative forms in the restricted dual
contents.reason: The source identifies the finite-tensor obstruction for the transposed multiplication; the local definition fixes the finite-codimensional-ideal convention and defers the coproduct until its image is proved to lie in A°⊗A°.

contents.name: §3.9 Lemma 3.47, Corollaries 3.49–3.50, and Lemmas 3.51–3.52: coefficient characterization and bialgebra/Hopf closure of the restricted dual
contents.reason: The source range supports the coefficient and closure claims; the carrier supplies complete local proofs, including finite-tensor separation and the antipode action on V*.

contents.name: §3.9 Theorems 3.45–3.46: the restricted dual coalgebra and Hopf algebra structures
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the stated structures from the finite-codimensional-ideal definition. The source gives only a sketch for Theorem 3.46; no missing proof step is imported.

contents.name: §3.9 Exercise 28: tensor-product Hopf structure and the restricted dual of the binomial Hopf algebra
contents.reason: The local example uses the tensor-product structure formulas, then computes its own basis formulas and verifies both antipode equations.

sources.title: Miguel Angelo Marques do Couto, Commutative-by-finite Hopf algebras and their finite dual, PhD thesis, University of Glasgow, 2019
sources.locator: Complete 222-page thesis; §1.3, Theorem 1.3.7(2) and its proof, Example 1.3.8, and Remark 1.3.9 (printed pp.21–23).

contents.name: Theorem 1.3.7(2), proof, Example 1.3.8, and Remark 1.3.9: finite dual of the primitive polynomial Hopf algebra
contents.reason: This independent treatment identifies all algebra maps k[x]→k as group-like elements of the finite dual and, in characteristic zero, gives k[x]° ≅ k[f] ⊗ k(k,+). It corroborates the source-convention discrepancy recorded in batch notes; the assigned carrier derives its all-characteristic point-indexed decomposition directly and does not rely on this result.
